evidence.requirements: Every requirement in the brief is met. The three tastings have the specified data (src/tastings.js:4-6). The start page shows the title, date and time, "EUR n per guest", "<n> seats left" and a "Book <title>" link (views.js:28-33; start.jpg). The form has fields labelled Name, Email and Guests (1 to 8) and a "Book" button (views.js:45-58). The seat limit is enforced in bookings.js:29-36. Errors appear above the fields inside the form card (views.js:44; form.jpg). The confirmation has the heading "Booking confirmed" and shows the tasting, guests, total and reference (views.js:72-78; confirmation.jpg). /staff has a Password field and a Sign in button, and the password comes from STAFF_PASSWORD (server.js:4, views.js:91-95). Staff see bookings grouped by tasting with name, email, guests, reference and a Cancel button (views.js:100-131; staff.jpg). Cancelling deletes the booking, which frees its seats (bookings.js:60-62). npm start honours PORT with a default of 3000 (server.js:3). Bookings are kept in memory and the interface is in English. No requirement is unmet.
evidence.correctness: Seat check and insert run synchronously in one call (bookings.js:28-46), so two concurrent requests cannot both take the last seat. Guests are validated with /^\d+$/ plus a 1–8 range (app.js:21), which rejects 0, 9, -1, 2.5, 1e1 and very large numbers (covered by test:121). Inputs that are not strings are coerced to '' (app.js:13), and name and email are trimmed and length-limited. Cancelling frees seats because seatsBooked is derived from the stored bookings (bookings.js:14-20). The error message distinguishes "fully booked" from "Only n seats are left". Booking references draw on 32 characters and 256 % 32 = 0, so there is no modulo bias; the generator retries on collision (bookings.js:64-71). Tastings that have already started are refused (app.js:109). Redirect-after-POST with 303 prevents double submits. A minor point: a fully booked tasting still shows its Book link and form, and the guest learns it is full only on submit.
evidence.security: All interpolated output goes through esc(), which covers & < > " ' (views.js:1-2), and an XSS test confirms this (test:240-253). The password is compared with timingSafeEqual over SHA-256 digests, and an empty STAFF_PASSWORD refuses sign-in (app.js:60-64). Session tokens are 32 random bytes kept server-side with an 8-hour expiry. The cookie is HttpOnly and SameSite=Strict, scoped to /staff, and destroyed on sign-out (app.js:150-163). Cancel checks the session (app.js:167). The CSP and nosniff headers are set and x-powered-by is disabled. No secrets are in the code. Gaps: there is no rate limiting or lockout on /staff/login, so the password can be brute-forced. The cookie has no Secure flag. Expired sessions are pruned only when they are looked up (app.js:52).
evidence.code_quality: Four small modules with clear responsibilities: tastings data, BookingStore, views, and an app factory with injectable password, store and clock (app.js:27-32). server.js is separate. Names are clear and validation sits in one function (app.js:15-25). Errors are handled with a dedicated BookingError type, unexpected errors are rethrown (app.js:122), and a 500 handler catches them. Comments are short and explain why. The size suits the task.
evidence.tests: There are 16 node:test tests (test/app.test.js) that run against a real HTTP server. They cover the start page contents, the form labels and button, the confirmation fields and total, filling a tasting exactly and overbooking it, the 8-guest boundary, many invalid guest values, name and email errors with values kept, 404s, past tastings (using an injected clock), the staff login page, a wrong password, grouping by tasting, cancel freeing seats, cancel without a session, sign-out, a forged cookie, an unset password and XSS escaping. Concurrent requests are not tested, but the synchronous design makes that low-risk.
evidence.ux_design: Screenshots show a clean, consistent wine-red theme with tasting cards, a clear booking form that keeps the guest's input and shows a visible error (form.jpg), a tidy confirmation summary with a monospaced reference (confirmation.jpg), and a staff page grouped into cards with "n of N seats booked" (staff.jpg). Weaknesses: dates appear in ISO format with no weekday ("2026-11-06 18:00"), which is less friendly for guests. The form does not show the running total. Cancel has no confirmation step, so one misclick deletes a booking. Fully booked tastings still show a Book button.
evidence.accessibility: All inputs have proper <label for> elements (views.js:46-56). The page sets lang="en" and uses semantic main, header, article, section and dl elements and tables with th. The error has role="alert" (views.js:44). The guests hint is linked with aria-describedby. Focus outlines are styled (style.css:81-84). Contrast is fine: muted #6e6360 on #fbf8f3 is about 5.5:1. Gaps: invalid fields carry no aria-invalid and are not linked to the error message, and focus is not moved to the error after the reload. Every staff Cancel button is labelled only "Cancel", with no accessible name for its booking. The action column header is empty (views.js:111).
evidence.simplicity: Express is the only runtime dependency. Pages are rendered with plain template-literal views and no template engine. Bookings are held in a Map, and cookies are parsed by hand in a few lines. The code totals about 450 lines including tests, which fits the task without needless abstraction.

strengths: Every requirement in the brief is met with exact labels and text, and the seat-limit, validation and cancellation logic is correct (bookings.js:28-46, app.js:15-25).
Solid security basics: escaping on every page, constant-time password comparison, random server-side session tokens with HttpOnly/SameSite=Strict cookies, and CSP headers.
A thorough integration test suite (16 tests) maps directly onto the brief's requirements and covers boundary, invalid and security cases.
issues: There is no rate limiting or lockout on POST /staff/login, so the single shared staff password can be brute-forced, and the session cookie has no Secure flag (app.js:146-157).

Accessibility gaps: form errors are not tied to their fields (no aria-invalid or aria-describedby on the field, and focus is not moved to the error), and every staff Cancel button is labelled only "Cancel" (views.js:44-56, 122).
UX rough edges: ISO dates with no weekday, Cancel deletes immediately with no confirmation, and fully booked tastings still offer a Book link and form (views.js:4, 33, 121-123).
review.verdict: This is a compact, well-structured and well-tested app that meets every requirement in the brief, handles seat limits and invalid input correctly, and covers the security basics. It could ship to the winery as is; adding login throttling, a cancel confirmation and better error association for screen readers would make it excellent.
